extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors planning and conducting systematic reviews (especially in health-related fields)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on where and how to prospectively register a planned systematic review, comparing registry features (costs, processing, searchability, metadata, sustainability) and alternative options for time-stamped protocol disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offering the service to prospectively register a systematic review
rubrics_metrics.description: Register must allow entering information about a planned systematic review into a database before starting the review process (i.e., prospective registration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Registration’ defined as entering information about a planned systematic review into a database before commencement; typically requires title, authors, planned methods, contact details. Distinguish registration from publishing a protocol (which may be peer-reviewed and indexed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing oversight and searchable coverage of registered reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Registry should provide oversight of registered systematic reviews, including searchable access to entries to help avoid unintended duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search functions are especially important to reduce duplicate reviews; authors should search bibliographic databases and registers before starting a review. The registry’s ability to surface similar ongoing reviews affects its utility for preventing research waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing time (turn-around time from submission to publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: How long it takes from submitting a registration to the record becoming visible/published in the registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some registries publish immediately (Research Registry), some promise short times (INPLASY: ≤48 hours), while others (PROSPERO) may take months due to eligibility/completeness checks. Faster turn-around is valued by authors but may be associated with fees or less curation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs / fees for registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registry charges authors to register, and how much.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free options (e.g., PROSPERO, OSF, protocols.io) vs paid services (Research Registry: £99; INPLASY: ~$20 initial). Authors must trade off cost against speed and curation; fees may be problematic for unfunded reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of records (checks for completeness and eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether submitted registration records are reviewed for completeness and eligibility before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO, Research Registry, and INPLASY perform checks (slows publication but may improve quality); OSF and protocols.io do not formally assess submissions. Assessment policies affect reliability and processing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields and structure (mandatory and optional metadata fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registry’s required data model: number and type of mandatory and optional fields (depth of information required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic-review-specific registries often have 24–28 mandatory fields (e.g., PROSPERO 28 mandatory + 12 optional). Generic registries may offer fewer structured fields or open-ended registration forms. A defined minimum dataset supports comparability and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search functionality and sophistication
rubrics_metrics.description: The registry’s search tools (text words, MeSH, investigator, title, identifiers) and how well they permit finding existing or similar registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO offers many search tools including MeSH but has been criticised as suboptimal. Search sophistication should ideally approach bibliographic database functionality to remain useful as the number of records grows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of contact details for corresponding author
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registry displays contact information for the registration’s corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three systematic-review-specific registries provide contact addresses; generic registries (OSF, protocols.io) may not. Contactability facilitates communication among researchers and resolving potential overlaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reminders and mechanisms to keep entries up to date
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registry actively prompts authors to update their record or has features encouraging up-to-date status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO provides reminders; for other registries this may be unclear or absent. Up-to-date records are important for accurate status and avoiding duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information on review status and linking to final publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registry records and displays review status (e.g., completed/published) and allows linking to or adding the DOI of the full paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO allows status information and adding links/DOIs once published; Research Registry allows uploading data files. Lack of status tracking reduces transparency about whether registered projects were completed and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction to systematic reviews (eligibility criteria for submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registry accepts only systematic reviews (and which types) or is open to all study designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registers vary: PROSPERO accepts only reviews with at least one direct health-related outcome; Research Registry accepts systematic reviews and meta-analyses; INPLASY accepts systematic and scoping reviews; OSF/protocols.io accept any study type. Authors must check eligibility rules before choosing a register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction to field/discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registry is limited to particular fields (e.g., health) or is discipline-agnostic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO is health-focused (but accepts related areas with direct health outcomes); others are open. Field restrictions determine whether a registry is appropriate for a given review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version tracking and ability to record updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registry supports versioning of registrations and tracking of changes over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO, INPLASY, OSF Registries, and protocols.io offer version tracking in differing ways. Versioning increases transparency about protocol changes and reduces concerns about post-hoc modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique identifying number and persistent identifier support
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registry assigns a unique identifier to each registration and/or provides DOIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO/Research Registry/INPLASY provide unique IDs; INPLASY, OSF, and protocols.io can provide DOIs for registrations. DOIs and unique IDs improve citability and tracing of registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to submit/upload results or associated data
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registry allows uploading study results, data files, or linking to an OSF project storing results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Registry allows uploading data files; OSF can link to project pages; most registries do not have a dedicated 'results' section. This feature affects whether the registry can serve as a full project repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate visibility vs post-publication curation model
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether submissions are made visible immediately and curated afterward, or are reviewed before visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Registry makes records visible immediately with curation after registration; INPLASY promises rapid publication; PROSPERO performs pre-publication checks and may delay visibility. Authors should weigh transparency (immediate visibility) against quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search usefulness for reducing duplication (practical effectiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: How useful the registry’s search function is in practice for identifying existing or similar registered reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although searchable, the actual practical utility of search functions is unclear for many registries. Poor searchability undermines the registry’s role in preventing duplicate reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popularity / coverage (number of registration records)
rubrics_metrics.description: The size and prominence of the registry as indicated by the number of registered records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO’s >100,000 records indicates prominence, but popularity may increase processing delays. Registry coverage affects the probability of finding existing similar work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host, founder, and governance (institutional backing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who hosts and runs the registry, and who founded or governs it (e.g., university, non-profit, for-profit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts include Centre for Reviews and Dissemination (PROSPERO), Research Registry (IJS Publishing Group), INPLASY (private), Center for Open Science (OSF), and protocols.io. Governance influences priorities, policies, and long-term stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and business model / sustainability risk
rubrics_metrics.description: How the registry is funded (government grant, non-profit, for-profit, fees) and the associated sustainability risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some registries are funded (PROSPERO by UK NIHR), some are for-profit (Research Registry, INPLASY), some non-profit (OSF). Funding instability (e.g., potential discontinuation) poses a risk to long-term access and performance; community discussion of fair financing is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to manage and share underlying project materials (project management features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the platform offers broader project management, data sharing, or repository features beyond a registration form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSF is a project management tool allowing storage and publication of data; Figshare/Zenodo provide time-stamped, version-tracked uploads with DOIs. Such features facilitate sharing of protocol documents and data alongside registration metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative time-stamped options (repositories and preregistration services)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-registry options to prospectively document planned methods: preprint/protocol publication, data repositories (OSF, Zenodo, Figshare), AsPredicted, PreregRS template, ClinicalTrials.gov (in some cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols in journals undergo peer review (quality assurance) and indexing (visibility). Repositories provide time-stamped, version-tracked DOIs; AsPredicted creates time-stamped PDFs that can remain private until revealed. Authors should consider these as complements or alternatives to formal registries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility specificity (e.g., requirement for direct health-related outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific eligibility rules that determine whether a given review can be registered in a registry (e.g., PROSPERO’s requirement for at least one direct health-related outcome).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must check registry-specific eligibility criteria; some registries exclude certain review types or topics, which may necessitate using a generic registry or alternative repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of DOI and citability of the registration record
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registry issues a DOI or other citable persistent identifier for the registration record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOIs (provided by INPLASY, OSF, protocols.io) facilitate citation and linking to protocol versions; absence of DOIs may reduce discoverability and formal citation of registered protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency trade-offs: speed vs curation vs cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The balance between rapid public disclosure, formal curation/quality checks, and any fees charged — and how this trade-off affects authors’ choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster, paid services may publish quickly but cost money; free registries may impose vetting delays. Authors should choose based on priorities (speed, cost, quality assurance, sustainability).
